summary.headline: Gallantt Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR111 crores (9.64% margin) from INR185 crores in Q1 on Gorakhpur shutdowns and power outage, with revenue flat at INR1,146 crores.
summary.overview: Revenue held at INR1,146 crores, up 13% year on year and flat quarter on quarter, as realisations offset lower volumes. TMT sales fell to 1,65,000 tons from about 1,92,000 tons in Q1 because of a planned Gorakhpur shutdown, and an unplanned extension of a captive power plant outage raised power costs. EBITDA margin compressed to 9.64% from 16.19% in Q1, and PAT fell to INR61 crores. Management attributes the hit to one-time factors and expects recovery from the Gorakhpur capacity ramp-up, power plant restart and higher steel prices in Q3. Coal block allotment in Singrauli and a medium-term greenfield growth plan (to be presented in Q4 FY27) were the main strategic updates.

segments.name: Gorakhpur (UP) integrated plant
segments.commentary: Planned shutdown to integrate expansion from 1.0 to 1.23 million tons; enhanced capacity expected operational around 10 November 2026, with 85-90% utilisation targeted by end-December. The captive power plant (78 MW, plus 22 MW being added) had an extended turbine-related outage, restart expected within a week.

segments.name: Kutch (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Rolling mill utilisation 68% in Q2 vs 66% in Q1, a 2 percentage point rise. Management expects further structural improvement in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: Captive power and renewables
segments.commentary: 18 MW solar at Siddhpur, Gujarat, complete and due to resume by November 2026; 60 MW solar at Prayagraj for Gorakhpur due Q4 FY27. Together expected to save INR30-40 crores per year in power cost.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 recovery expected from Gorakhpur capacity, power plant restart and firmer steel prices; management says price increase of about 20-21% (TMT, September vs a year ago) only reflected from September, so benefit lands mainly in Q3.
Working capital (inventory) expected to normalise in Q3 once new Gorakhpur capacity is operational within 15-20 days.

Remaining FY27 capex of around INR500 crores, split INR400 crores Gorakhpur, INR240 crores mines, INR170 crores solar and INR100 crores Kutch, all to be funded from internal accruals. Note the split sums to more than INR500 crores as stated on the call.
Iron ore blocks targeted operational in FY28; captive mines expected to add about INR2,000 per ton to EBITDA once fully utilised, with partial feed in the first one to two years.
Medium-term greenfield growth plan, built around iron ore and coal blocks, to be presented in Q4 FY27; funding mix (internal accruals vs debt/equity) not yet decided.
Management expects utilisation to improve by 3-5% next year as shutdowns are synchronised and capacity is added.
capex_capacity: Gorakhpur expansion from 1.0 to 1.23 million tons; enhanced capacity expected operational around 10 November 2026. Management also referenced a 1.3 million ton annual target. Gorakhpur capacity addition at every stage except sponge iron, including 22 MW additional generation to the 78 MW captive plant.

Singrauli coal block allotted August 2026; due diligence under way with a one-month decision window. Operations would take about 2-3 years after a decision; Gorakhpur intended to move fully to this coal, replacing imported South African coal.
Iron ore blocks in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan: exploration in progress, environment and forest clearances underway, FY28 target.
Gujarat: captive power debottlenecking completed in the last month (results in Q3); sponge iron (DRI) plant to commission in Q4 FY27, with benefits from next financial year.
Power outsourcing after the 22 MW addition is about 5-7 MW, to be covered by the 60 MW Prayagraj solar plant in Q4; until then 5-6 MW bought from grid and exchange.
demand_pricing: Management says India finished steel consumption grew 7.5% to about 85 million tons in H1; construction steel demand up about 7% per management. India remained a net importer of finished steel.

TMT prices in September were about 21% higher than a year ago; management says finished product prices rose about 20% while raw material cost rose about INR3,000 per ton in Q2 (coal about INR2,500 per ton, iron ore about 1%).
Brand premium: management says it commands 5-6% over unbranded TMT in UP and 3-4% in Gujarat; Ajay Devgn endorsement (four years) and Janhvi Kapoor recently added.
Gallantt Advance submersible: more than 25% share of the submersible market in UP, per management.
Management expects prices to stay firm into the November-December construction peak, though part of the price gain is being passed on to energy costs.

qa_highlights.question: What does the Singrauli coal block mean strategically and how does it change cost position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the block was only just allotted and is in due diligence; iron ore blocks are targeted for FY28, and securing both raw materials is a basis for the next growth phase.

qa_highlights.question: How will the medium-term growth plan be funded: internal accruals or debt and equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Vice Chairman Dindayal Jalan said the mix is undecided and depends on project size; the company historically relies on internal accruals and limited external borrowing.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are TMT prices into the construction season, and what is seen in October?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects prices to remain strong as construction peaks from November-December, with some part of the gain absorbed by energy costs. Price rise came mainly in September, so the effect lands in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 margin fall is due to shutdowns versus input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited both shutdowns and coal price increases (about 4.5-5% of revenue) with realisations lagging; the price rise only came through in September, so Q2 saw little benefit.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the price premium over unbranded TMT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 5-6% premium in UP and 3-4% in Gujarat, sustained by branding and dealer network.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise by about INR118 crores in H1 and when does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory build came from the prolonged shutdown during hookup of new capacity and stock built to supply added capacity; expected to normalise in Q3 once the plant is running.

qa_highlights.question: What is the remaining FY27 capex and how is it funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Jalan said about INR500 crores remains for FY27 (INR400 crores Gorakhpur, INR240 crores mines, INR170 crores solar, INR100 crores Kutch), funded from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: How fast will Gorakhpur ramp up and what utilisation to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up takes one to one-and-a-half months to reach 85-90% utilisation; start proposed 10 November, so stable running by December end.

risks_watch: Q3 margin recovery depends on Gorakhpur commissioning on schedule (10 November target) and the captive power plant restarting within a week of the call; management noted minor commissioning issues could arise.
Input cost pressure: coal and freight remain elevated, with raw material cost up about INR3,000 per ton in Q2 while finished prices lagged until September.
Iron ore captive mine (FY28 target) and coal block (2-3 years after decision) are not yet operational; the INR2,000 per ton EBITDA benefit is a forward estimate and is not yet secured.
Medium-term greenfield project to be presented in Q4 FY27; size, capex, land and state incentives and funding mix (accruals vs debt/equity) are undecided.
Working capital: inventory rose to INR669 crores; normalisation in Q3 is management's expectation and needs to be verified.
Kutch rolling mill utilisation only 68%; management expects improvement but the monsoon-season demand dip in Q3 may limit it.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term story (integration, capacity, brand) but explicitly defensive on Q2, attributing the margin drop to one-time shutdowns and a power outage. Management was forward-looking on Q3 recovery but gave several timelines loosely and deferred the growth plan and funding decisions to Q4 FY27.
